We report results of a variety of automatic evaluation metrics used in the past studies to provide a comprehensive comparison of existing methods and our proposed method.

We include fact‑verification based metrics, NLI‑Acc, which specifically aims to evaluate the faithfulness of the sentences. We also report string‑based metrics that evaluate the string match between predictions and references, such as sacre‑BLEU, ROUGE-{1,2,L}, TER, METEOR, PARENT, and NE‑based metrics (RC, RI, MI, etc.).

We asked three human evaluators to evaluate 200 samples of each dataset (100 samples in each of the overlap/nonoverlap split for ToTTo), and each sample is provided with all the inputs, the reference, and two system generated sentences.
guideline: evaluation based on faithfulness and adequacy criteria
Evaluators judged each generated sentence for (1) faithfulness (all facts entailed by the input) and (2) adequacy (covers same or more facts than the reference).
